name: room
text: Room opened — goal: improve: Self-improvement: review prompts/engines/routing/own-code; auto-apply safe changes; pitch

name: Sprocket
text:
DO: Replace the current prompt-review system with a shared log that records every change to prompts, engines, and routing rules.

This log makes all changes transparent and auditable, cutting review time from days to minutes. The trade-off is a one-time setup cost for the logging system and a small ongoing storage overhead.

name: Gauge
text: A shared log risks becoming a graveyard of stale noise, where changes pile up and reasons for modifications get lost. This could lead to a cascade of silent misalignments, making it harder to track the impact of changes over time. Instead of a shared log, we could implement a version-controlled system that auto-applies safe changes and requires manual review for riskier modifications, which would allow us to weigh the benefits of transparency against the dangers of information overload.
